title: Flag exceptional multi-month/delayed payments for warden review
description: Occasionally a tenant delays a month and later pays for two months together in one lump sum. This is a legitimate but exceptional pattern that today just looks like two ordinary payments - the warden has no way to spot it happened, or reconcile it, later. Resolved design question: today a Payment is tied to exactly one Invoice (LODGY-17), so 'one transaction clearing two periods' isn't expressible yet - this needs a real flow to record one payment and apply/split it across multiple invoices at once (not just a same-day-multiple-payments heuristic). Confirmed low priority/rare in practice, so this can wait behind higher-value tickets.
acceptanceCriteria: Warden can record one payment amount and apply it across more than one of a tenant's unpaid/partial invoices in a single action, rather than recording separate payments per invoice
Each invoice's paid-so-far amount updates correctly from its share of the single payment
The resulting multi-period payment is flagged/labeled as such on the invoice(s) and payment record
Dashboard or payment list surfaces these flagged multi-period payments so a warden can review them
No change to how a normal single-period payment is recorded or displayed

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Resolved the schema gap flagged in backlog review: build the real one-payment-across-multiple-invoices flow (not a lighter heuristic). Downgraded Medium -> Low since this is rare in practice - fine to sit behind higher-value tickets.

Starting - one lump sum split across several of a tenant's open invoices. Adding a nullable multiPeriodGroupId to Payment (DB v4) so the several rows a single transaction produces stay linked and flaggable, rather than inferring it from same-day heuristics; single-period recording is untouched.

One lump sum can now be applied across several of a tenant's open months in a single action. Payment gained a nullable multiPeriodGroupId (DB v4, MIGRATION_3_4 is a plain ADD COLUMN); every row a single transaction writes shares one generated id, which is what makes the payment recognisable afterwards as one lump sum - a real link in the data, not the same-day heuristic the ticket ruled out. data/PaymentAllocation.kt holds the split as a pure function: oldest period first, each month settled in full before the next gets anything, which is how a warden describes it ('this clears August and part of September') and the only split that leaves an unambiguous trail; money beyond every outstanding balance is dropped rather than parked on the last invoice, since the app has no unallocated-balance concept and overpaying one month would make that invoice's own arithmetic wrong. MultiPeriodPaymentScreen (from the tenant profile) lists the open months oldest-first with each one's outstanding figure, prefills the total needed to clear them all, and shows the split live as the amount is edited, so nothing is applied by surprise. Outstanding is computed through effectiveAmountDue(), so a credited month asks for less. On save each invoice gets its own payment row and its own status recalculated from its own share - August PAID and September PARTIAL out of one transaction. Fewer than two open months refuses outright and points the warden at the ordinary flow, so AC 5 holds: single-period recording is untouched, and RecordPaymentViewModel still writes multiPeriodGroupId null by default. Surfaced on the invoice list: any invoice funded by a grouped payment carries a 'Part of a multi-month payment' line. Tests: PaymentAllocationTest for the split (exact, partial, over-payment, already-settled rows, empty cases); MultiPeriodPaymentViewModelTest for ordering and prefill, settled months excluded, the single-month refusal, one shared group id across rows, per-invoice status derivation, credits reducing a month's share, and zero being refused. testDebugUnitTest green (349 tests).

PASS - all five, verified against the database. Set Ramesh up with three open invoices (5/2026 2200 after credit, 6/2026 6000, 7/2026 6000). AC1: 'Pay several months at once' takes one amount and applies it across them in a single action; entering 10000 instead of the prefilled 14200 recalculated the preview live to 2200 + 6000 + 1800, oldest first. AC2: after saving, each invoice's paid-so-far was correct - 5/2026 PAID, 6/2026 PAID, 7/2026 PARTIAL showing '1800 of 6000'. AC3: all three payment rows share one multiPeriodGroupId and each invoice row is labelled 'Part of a multi-month payment'. AC4: the payment list surfaces that label on every affected invoice, so the warden can spot and review them. AC5: recorded an ordinary single payment on a fresh 8/2026 invoice - it saved through the unchanged Record Payment screen, its payment row has multiPeriodGroupId NULL, and the invoice shows Paid with no multi-month label.
